answer: Ecological Attention Lease. Each identity must continuously hold a unique, sensor-verified attention record tied to a physical site: a terrace, a grove, or a meadow, assigned by lot. Enforcement requires periodic liveness proofs from that site's ambient sensors, with readings cross-checked against neighbors. A sybil cannot reuse one site across identities, so each extra identity demands a separately maintained physical location and fresh sensor hardware, raising per-identity cost to real estate plus continuous upkeep.
